stem:
A school tested a quiet lunch room for one week. Twenty students used it daily and most said it helped them relax. However, students chose whether to participate, and the school collected no information from those who stayed away. The head teacher decided to continue the trial before making a permanent change.
Can we conclude that the quiet room benefits every student? Answer and cite the strongest limitation in the text.
key: No. The evidence comes from self-selected participants, not all students; nonparticipants were not surveyed. Most is not every. Accept either well-explained textual limitation without inventing opposite results.
rubric: 否定全体受益这一过度概括
提供自选参与／未调查未参加者的文本证据
不把未证明全体受益说成证明无效

stem:
Write a 35–50-word summary of this original training passage. The word limit is a practice setting, not an official exam rule.
For years, a town library closed at six in the evening. Residents who worked during the day often said that they could visit only on Saturdays. In response, the library tested a later closing time for one month, keeping its doors open until eight on weekdays. Posters at bus stops and notices on the library website announced the trial.
During that month, evening visits increased. Many of the additional visitors were daytime workers who came to borrow books or use the computers after work. One visitor said that she could now collect books on her way home instead of making a separate weekend trip.
However, the trial created difficulties for staff. No extra workers had been hired, so the existing team covered the longer schedule. Several employees reported feeling tired, especially when they had to close the building and return early the next morning.
The library therefore has not promised to make the change permanent. It will continue the later opening hours only if the town provides enough money for another evening shift. A decision on that funding is still pending.
key: Cover the later-opening trial and increased access/visits, the staffing burden, and the funding condition for continuation. Possible 43-word version: A month-long trial of later library hours increased evening visits, particularly among daytime workers. However, the change tired existing staff because no extra workers were hired. Continuing the extended schedule therefore depends on the town funding an additional evening shift to support it.
rubric: 覆盖延时试行及访问增加，筛去宣传渠道／访客个例等次要细节
保留人手不足／疲劳问题
保留继续延时的经费条件，不误写为已决定永久实行
独立整合表述并遵守本题训练词数

stem:
This is one sentence-insertion micro-task, not a full six-choose-four paper.
Students first listed the problems they noticed on their walk to school. [GAP] Finally, they compared the proposals and chose one they could complete in a month.
Which sentence fits best? A. They then worked in pairs to suggest solutions to those problems. B. The school had opened fifty years earlier. C. Walking is sometimes faster than taking a bus.
key: A. first/then/finally and problems → solutions/proposals establish the sequence and reference. B and C do not bridge the stated stages.
rubric: 选择 A
说明至少一个跨句照应和过程顺序，不靠主题词碰运气
